title: Driver Breaks During the Round
question: On the 7th hole, your driver shaft snaps after you hit a tee shot. The damage occurred during the normal course of play. What are you allowed to do?

choices.text: Continue using the damaged club if possible.
Replace the damaged club with another club.

explanation: If a club is damaged during the normal course of play, you may continue using the club in its damaged state, repair it provided you do not unduly delay play, or replace it with another club as long as obtaining a replacement does not result in unreasonable delay or borrowing from another player on the course. (Rule 4.1a(2))

juniorVersion.title: What Can You Do If Your Driver Breaks?
juniorVersion.question: You hit a big drive on the 7th hole and your driver stick snaps. It broke while you were playing. What are you allowed to do next?

choices.text: Keep using the broken driver if you can.
Swap your broken driver for a different club.
You can do any of these things.

juniorVersion.explanation: If your club breaks while you are playing, you can use it broken, fix it, or get another one, as long as you do not make everyone wait a long time or borrow from someone else playing with you.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A big club used to hit the ball a long way, usually from the tee at the start of a hole.
The long stick part of the club that you hold.
The first hit you take to start a hole.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show an example of a club with a broken shaft. Ask children what they think they can do, then explain the rule step-by-step.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they can only fix or only swap the club, not use it broken.
Children may think they have to get rid of the broken club right away.
